p.src: Xiren asked Pinger what had caused all the commotion. Pinger laughed. “It is something no one in the world could have imagined, and quite amusing when told. I’ll tell you in a few days. It’s all still in a muddle, and I have no time just now.” Before she had finished, a maid of Li Wan’s arrived and said, “Sister Pinger, so you are here! Mistress is waiting for you. Why haven’t you come?” Pinger hurriedly turned to leave, calling with a laugh, “I’m coming, I’m coming.” Xiren and the others laughed. “Now that her mistress is ill, she has become such a prized morsel that everyone is clamouring for her.” We need say no more of Pinger after she left.

p.src: Baoyu then called to Chunyan, “Go with your mother to Miss Bao’s rooms and say a few conciliatory words to Yinger. You mustn’t offend her without making amends.” Chunyan agreed and went out with her mother. Baoyu called through the window after them, “Don’t say it in front of Miss Bao, or Yinger may get a scolding instead.”

p.src: Mother and daughter answered and went on their way, chatting as they walked. Chunyan said to her mother, “I was always advising you, but you would never listen. Why did you have to make such a scene and humiliate yourself before you would stop?” Her mother laughed. “Off with you, you little hussy! As the saying goes, ‘Experience teaches wisdom.’ Now I understand. You needn’t come interrogating me again.” Chunyan laughed. “Mother, if you behave yourself and remain in this household for a long time, there will naturally be many benefits for you. Let me tell you something: Baoyu often says that in future he intends to ask Her Ladyship to release every one of us serving in these rooms, whether our families belong to the household or live outside it, so that we may return to our own parents and choose our own course. Tell me, isn’t that alone a wonderful thing?” Delighted to hear this, her mother hurriedly asked, “Is that really true?” “Why would anyone make up such a lie?” replied Chunyan. On hearing this, the old woman invoked the Buddha’s name over and over.

p.src: Presently they reached Allspice Court, where Baochai, Daiyu, Aunt Xue and the others happened to be dining. Yinger had gone to make tea, so Chunyan and her mother went straight to her and said with conciliatory smiles, “Our words were rude just now. Please don’t be angry or take offence; we have come especially to apologize,” and more to that effect. Yinger promptly smiled, offered them seats, and poured them tea. Mother and daughter said they had business to attend to, took their leave, and started back. Suddenly Ruiguan came running after them, calling, “Auntie! Sister! Please wait a moment.” Coming up to them, she handed them a paper packet, saying it contained rose-nitre and asking them to take it to Fangguan for her face. Chunyan laughed. “How petty you two are! Do you suppose there isn’t any there for her? Yet you have gone specially to make up another packet for her.” “What she has there is hers,” said Ruiguan. “What I give her is mine. Dear sister, please be sure to take it back to her.” Chunyan had no choice but to accept it. When mother and daughter returned, Jia Huan and Jia Cong had just arrived to inquire after Baoyu and had only just gone inside. Chunyan said to her mother, “I’ll go in by myself. You needn’t come, Mother.” Her mother obeyed her in everything from then on and no longer dared to be obstinate.

p.src: When Chunyan entered, Baoyu knew she had come to report back and nodded before she could speak. Understanding his meaning, Chunyan said not a word. After standing there briefly, she turned and went out, signalling to Fangguan with her eyes. When Fangguan came out, Chunyan quietly told her about Ruiguan and gave her the rose-nitre. Baoyu had nothing to discuss with Jia Cong and Jia Huan, so he smiled and asked what Fangguan was holding. Fangguan promptly handed it to Baoyu to inspect and explained that it was rose-nitre for treating spring rash. Baoyu laughed. “How thoughtful of her!” Hearing this, Jia Huan craned his neck to look and caught a whiff of its delicate fragrance. Bending down, he pulled a sheet of paper from the leg of his boot, held it out, and said with a smile, “Dear brother, give me half.” Baoyu had no choice but to give him some. But Fangguan, unwilling to share Ruiguan’s gift with anyone else, hurriedly stopped him and said with a smile, “Don’t touch this. I’ll fetch you some other.” Baoyu understood and quickly wrapped it up again, saying, “Hurry and fetch it.”

p.src: Fangguan took the packet away and put it safely aside, then went to her dressing case to find the powder she normally used. When she opened the case, however, the box was empty. She was puzzled: there had still been some left that morning, so how had it disappeared? When she asked the others, they all said they knew nothing about it. Sheyue said, “This is no time to make a fuss asking about that. Someone in these rooms must simply have run short and taken it. Whatever you give those two, how could they possibly tell the difference? Hurry and send them on their way, so that we can have our meal.” Taking her advice, Fangguan made up a packet of jasmine powder and brought it out. As soon as Jia Huan saw it, he reached out to take it. Fangguan promptly tossed it onto the kang. Jia Huan had no choice but to pick it up from the kang and tuck it inside his robe before taking his leave.

p.src: As Jia Zheng was away from home, and Lady Wang and the others were also absent, Jia Huan had been feigning illness and playing truant for several days. Now that he had obtained the powder, he went eagerly to find Caiyun. Caiyun happened to be chatting with Concubine Zhao. Grinning, Jia Huan said to Caiyun, “I have obtained a packet of something fine too. It is for you to put on your face. You are always saying that rose-nitre cures ringworm better than the silver powder sold outside. Take a look and see whether this is the stuff.” Caiyun opened it, took one look, and burst out laughing. “Who did you get this from?” she asked. Jia Huan told her what had just happened. Caiyun laughed. “They have been making a country bumpkin of you. This is not nitre at all; it is jasmine powder.” Jia Huan examined it and saw that it was indeed rather redder than the powder he had seen before; when he sniffed it, it was richly fragrant too. He laughed and said, “It is good stuff all the same. Powder is powder, so keep it for your face. Anything from here must surely be better than what they sell outside.” Caiyun had no choice but to accept it. Concubine Zhao said, “So much for giving you something fine! Who told you to go begging for it? How can you blame them for making a fool of you? If it were up to me, I would take it back and fling it in her face. Now is the time, while those who go gallivanting are out gallivanting and those confined to bed are still in bed. Make a proper scene, so that no one else can enjoy any peace either; that will settle the score. Surely they are not going to dig up this grievance two months from now and call you to account for it? Even if they do question you, you will have an answer. Baoyu is your elder brother, so I can understand your not daring to cross him. But surely that does not mean you dare not even go and question the cats and dogs in his rooms!” At this, Jia Huan lowered his head. Caiyun hurriedly said, “Why stir up trouble over this? Whatever has happened, we had better bear it patiently.” “Stay out of it,” said Concubine Zhao. “It has nothing to do with you anyway. Now that we have right on our side, it would do some good to give those wanton sluts a thorough scolding.” Then, pointing at Jia Huan, she cried, “Pah! You spineless, good-for-nothing wretch! You deserve to be bullied by those little brats! If I so much as say a word to you, or accidentally hand you the wrong thing, you turn on your own mother, veins bulging, eyes glaring, stamping and flinging things about. Yet now you let that pack of little bitches make a fool of you and do nothing. And you still expect the servants in this household to fear you in future! You have not a scrap of manhood, and even I am ashamed for you.” Jia Huan was both ashamed and angry when he heard this, but still dared not go. He merely flung out his hands and said, “You talk so bravely, yet you do not dare go yourself; you only send me to make trouble. If they report me to the school and I am beaten, do you think it will not hurt you too? Every time, you incite me to start a quarrel; but when trouble comes of it and I am beaten and scolded, you hang your head just the same. And now you are inciting me to quarrel with those little maids again. If you are not afraid of Third Sister, go yourself; then I will admit you are brave.”

p.src: That one remark struck his mother to the heart. She shouted, “She came out of my own belly! Why should I be afraid of her? This household has become more outrageous than ever!” As she spoke, she snatched up the packet and flew off toward the Garden. Caiyun pleaded with her desperately but could not stop her, and finally hid in another room. Jia Huan likewise slipped out beyond the ceremonial gate and went off to amuse himself.

p.src: Concubine Zhao marched straight into the Garden, seething with anger, and there ran headlong into Dame Xia, Ouguan’s foster mother, coming the other way. Seeing Concubine Zhao approaching in a fury, Dame Xia asked, “Where are you off to, ma’am?” Concubine Zhao said, “Just look at this! Even those little play-acting trollops who have only been in the household a day or two have learned to treat people differently according to their standing and serve them on different-sized dishes. If it were anyone else, I might not be so angry; but if I let those little whores make a fool of me, what would become of my dignity?” This was exactly what Dame Xia wanted to hear, and she eagerly asked what had happened. Concubine Zhao told her the whole story of how Fangguan had insulted Jia Huan by passing off face powder as nitre. Dame Xia said, “Good gracious, ma’am! Have you only found out today? This is nothing at all. Only yesterday they privately burned spirit money in this very place, and Baoyu even stepped forward to shield them. Before anyone else has even brought anything in, they say it must not be allowed because it would be unclean and unlucky. Yet there is nothing unlucky about burning spirit money? Think about it, ma’am: apart from Her Ladyship, who in this household outranks you? It is only because you fail to assert yourself. If you stood up for yourself properly, who would not fear you? Here is what I think: these little actresses are not truly members of the household, so there is little harm in offending them. Seize on these two incidents as grounds for making an example of them. I will stand witness beside you, while you show them your authority; then it will be easier for you to uphold your rights in other matters too. Even the young mistresses and ladies could hardly take the side of those little actresses against you.” These words made Concubine Zhao feel more justified than ever. “I know nothing about the burning of spirit money,” she said. “Tell me exactly what happened.” Dame Xia related the entire earlier incident, detail by detail, and added, “Go ahead and speak your mind. If a quarrel breaks out, we shall be there to support you.” Hearing this, Concubine Zhao became more pleased with herself than ever. Emboldened, she went straight on to Happy Red Court.

p.src: As it happened, Baoyu heard that Daiyu was there and went off to see her. Fangguan was eating with Xiren and the others. When they saw Concubine Zhao arrive, they all rose and smilingly invited her to join them. “Do have something to eat, Auntie. What has brought you here in such a hurry?” Concubine Zhao made no reply. She strode forward and flung the powder into Fangguan’s face, pointing at her as she cursed, “You filthy little whore! You were bought with our money to learn opera; you’re no better than a common singing-girl or prostitute! Even the lowest servants in our household are more respectable than you, yet you know very well how to serve people according to their rank. When Baoyu wanted to give him something, you stepped in to stop him—as though it belonged to you! You tried to fob him off with this, thinking he wouldn’t know the difference! Whatever else may be said, they are brother and sister and equally your masters. What right have you to look down on him?” Fangguan could not bear such abuse. Weeping, she protested, “I gave him this only because there was no rose powder left. If I had simply said there was none, I was afraid he would not believe me. Besides, isn’t this good powder too? I may have learned opera, but I never went out to perform in public. I’m only a young girl—what would I know about singing-whores and prostitutes? There is no call for you to come and abuse me, Auntie. Your household was not the one that bought me. As the saying goes, ‘When maidservants swear sisterhood, they are slaves together!’” Xiren hurriedly pulled her back. “Don’t talk such nonsense!” she said. Enraged, Concubine Zhao rushed forward and slapped Fangguan twice across the face. Xiren and the others hurried over to restrain and pacify her. “Please don’t lower yourself by quarreling with a child, Auntie. Leave her to us; we shall speak to her.” After taking those two blows, Fangguan had no intention of letting the matter rest. She threw herself down, rolled about, and began to scream and wail. “What makes you think you have the right to hit me?” she cried. Take a look at yourself before you raise your hand against me! If I let you beat me without resisting, I might as well not go on living!” With that, she hurled herself against Concubine Zhao, daring her to strike again. The others tried at once to reason with Fangguan and pull her away. Qingwen quietly tugged at Xiren and said, “Leave them alone. Let them make a scene and see how they get out of it! Chaos rules nowadays: first one person comes to beat her, then another. If everyone starts behaving like this, what will become of us?”

p.src: At that moment Ouguan and Ruiguan were amusing themselves together. Kui官, the painted-face actress assigned to Xiangyun, and Douguan, who belonged to Baoqin, heard the news and hurried to find them. “Fangguan is being bullied,” they said. “It is a disgrace to all of us. We must all go and make a tremendous scene if we are to vindicate ourselves.” The four were children at heart. Thinking only of their loyal indignation on Fangguan’s behalf and heedless of everything else, they all rushed into Happy Red Court. Douguan charged headfirst and nearly knocked Concubine Zhao off her feet. The other three crowded in as well, wailing at the tops of their voices, clawing with their hands and butting with their heads until they had Concubine Zhao completely surrounded. Qingwen and the others laughed as they made a show of trying to pull them away. Poor Xiren hauled one girl to her feet only for another to dart away, crying all the while, “Are you trying to get yourselves killed? If you have been wronged, you may state your grievance. How can you do something so utterly unreasonable?” Concubine Zhao, for her part, completely lost her bearings and could do nothing but curse wildly. Ruiguan and Ouguan seized one arm apiece, while Kui官 and Douguan butted against her from front and back. All four kept crying, “You may as well beat the four of us to death!” Fangguan lay rigid on the floor, having cried herself into a faint.

Concubine Zhao, for her part, completely lost her bearings and could do nothing but curse wildly.
Ruiguan and Ouguan seized one arm apiece, while Kui官 and Douguan butted against her from front and back.
All four kept crying, “You may as well beat the four of us to death!”
Fangguan lay rigid on the floor, having cried herself into a faint.

p.src: While the uproar showed no sign of ending, it turned out that Qingwen had already sent Chunyan to report the matter to Tanchun. Presently Madam You, Li Wan, and Tanchun arrived with Pinger and a group of married servants and shouted the four girls into submission. When they asked what had happened, Concubine Zhao glared furiously, the veins standing out on her forehead, and tried unsuccessfully to give a coherent account of the whole affair. Madam You and Li Wan did not respond, but merely ordered the four girls to desist. Tanchun sighed. “What great matter is this, that you should become so angry over it, Auntie? I have something I was just wishing to discuss with you. No wonder the maids could not tell me where you were—you were here losing your temper. Come with me at once.” Madam You and Li Wan both smiled. “Please come into the hall, Auntie, and let us talk things over.”

p.src: Concubine Zhao had no choice but to accompany the three of them, though she continued muttering complaints as she went. Tanchun said, “Those little girls are really no more than playthings. When you are pleased with them, you may joke and laugh with them; when you are not, you need only ignore them. Even if one of them misbehaves, it is no worse than being scratched or bitten by a kitten or puppy. Forgive her if you can; if you cannot, you should summon the stewardesses, explain the matter, and have them punish her. Why demean yourself by shouting and bawling and forgetting your dignity? Look at Concubine Zhou. Why does no one bully her? Because she does not go looking for quarrels. I advise you to return to your room and cool your temper. Do not listen to the prompting of those wretches. You will only make yourself a laughingstock, foolishly doing their dirty work for nothing. Even if you are bursting with anger, endure it for these few days. When Madam returns, she will naturally settle the matter.” This speech left Concubine Zhao without a word to say, and she had no alternative but to return to her room.

p.src: Tanchun, still angry, said to Madam You and Li Wan, “She is so old, yet nothing she does inspires anyone’s respect. What is the sense of making such an uproar over a trifle, with no thought for dignity? She is easily swayed and has no judgment of her own. This must be the prompting of those shameless servants. They have made a fool of her and used her to vent their own spite.” The more she thought about it, the angrier she became, and she ordered an inquiry into who had instigated the affair. The married servants had no choice but to obey. Once outside, they exchanged smiles and said, “How are we to find a needle in the ocean?” They could only summon Concubine Zhao’s attendants and the people in the garden for questioning, but all denied knowing anything. Unable to discover anything, they reported to Tanchun, “It is difficult to find out at once. We shall investigate gradually, and whenever anyone is found to have caused trouble with improper talk, we shall report it and have the offender punished.”

p.src: Only when Tanchun's anger had gradually subsided did the matter come to an end. Just then, Aiguan quietly reported to Tanchun, “Mother Xia has always been at odds with us and is forever spreading tales and stirring up trouble. The other day she made trouble over Ouguan's burning paper money; luckily Baoyu had told her to burn it and admitted as much himself, so Mother Xia had nothing more to say. Today, when I went to deliver a handkerchief for you, I saw her whispering with Aunt Zhao for ages; they did not move apart until they saw me.” Though Tanchun understood that something underhand was going on, she also judged that they were all of one faction and equally prone to outrageous mischief. She merely acknowledged the report and would not accept it as proven fact.

p.src: Now, as it happened, Mother Xia's granddaughter, Chan'er, worked in Tanchun's quarters. She often bought things and summoned servants for the maids there, and all the girls were fond of her. After the meal that day, Tanchun went to the hall to attend to business, while Cuimo stayed behind to mind the rooms. She told Chan'er to go out and have a young servant buy some cakes. Chan'er said, “I have just swept that enormous garden, and my back and legs are aching. Send someone else.” Cuimo laughed. “Who else am I to send? Hurry along. I have something useful to tell you: when you pass the rear gate, warn your grandmother to be on her guard.” She then repeated what Aiguan had said about Chan'er's grandmother. Hearing this, Chan'er hurriedly took the money and said, “So that little wretch wants to make trouble for people too! Just wait till I report this.” With that, she rose and went out. When she reached the rear gate, she saw that work in the kitchen had slackened and everyone was sitting on the stone steps chatting. Her grandmother was among them. Chan'er ordered one of the old women to go out and buy the cakes. Then, cursing as she spoke, she told Mother Xia what she had just heard. Mother Xia was both angry and frightened. She wanted to seek out Aiguan and question her, and also to go before Tanchun to protest her innocence. Chan'er hurriedly stopped her. “What could you possibly say if you went there? How would you explain learning of this? You would only make matters worse by dragging it all into the open. I told you only so you could be on your guard. There is no need to rush into anything this very moment.”

p.src: As they were speaking, Fangguan suddenly appeared. Leaning against the courtyard gate, she called laughingly to Liu's wife in the kitchen, “Sister Liu, Second Master Bao says he wants something cool and tart among his vegetarian dishes for supper. Just don't add sesame oil and make it greasy.” Liu's wife laughed. “I understand. Fancy sending you today to deliver such an important message! If you don't mind the dirt, why not come in and look around?” Fangguan had just entered when an old woman appeared carrying a plate of cakes. Fangguan teased, “Who bought those hot cakes? Let me taste one first.” Chan'er snatched the plate with one hand and said, “Someone else bought these. Surely you people don't hanker after such things.” Seeing this, Liu's wife hurriedly smiled and said, “Miss Fang, do you like these? I have some that I just bought for your sister. She has not eaten them, and they are still put away, perfectly clean and untouched.” As she spoke, she brought out a plate and handed it to Fangguan, adding, “Wait here while I go in and brew you a cup of good tea.” She went inside and immediately opened the stove to heat water for the tea. Holding the hot cakes close to Chan'er's face, Fangguan said, “As if I coveted your cakes! Aren't these cakes too? I was only joking. Even if you kowtowed to me, I would not eat yours.” She then broke the cakes apart one by one and tossed the pieces at sparrows for sport, laughing as she said, “Sister Liu, don't begrudge them. I'll buy you two catties later.” Little Chan was speechless with rage. She glared at Fangguan and sneered, “Even the Lord of Thunder has eyes—why doesn't he strike down such a wicked creature? And she has the gall to taunt me! How could I compare with you people? Some bring you tribute, others make abject slaves of themselves, flattering you in every way so that you will put in a good word for them.” The married women all said, “Come now, girls, that's enough. You bicker every single time you meet.” Several of the more perceptive women, seeing the two had begun trading words and fearing further trouble, got to their feet and went their separate ways. Chan'er did not dare say too much more to Fangguan and went away grumbling.

p.src: Liu's wife, it should be explained, had a daughter who was just sixteen that year. Though she was a kitchen servant's child, her looks could compare with those of Ping'er, Xiren, Zijuan, and Ying'er. As she was the fifth child, she was called Wu'er, or Fifth Daughter. She had always been frail and therefore had not been assigned any duties. Recently, however, Liu's wife had noticed that the maids in Baoyu's apartments had light duties and plenty of company; moreover, she had heard that Baoyu intended eventually to set them all free. She therefore wanted to have her daughter placed there in name. She had no means of arranging it, but fortunately she herself served at Pear-Fragrance Court. She was exceptionally attentive and obliging and waited on Fangguan and the other girls better than their own foster mothers did. Fangguan and the others were equally kind to mother and daughter. Liu's wife had now spoken to Fangguan about the matter and asked her to intercede with Baoyu. Although Baoyu had agreed, he had lately been ill and beset by many affairs, so the matter had not yet been settled.

p.src: But enough of what came before. Fangguan now returned to Happy-Red Court and reported back to Baoyu. Baoyu had been displeased when he heard Aunt Zhao quarreling. It had seemed wrong either to intervene or to remain silent, so he had waited until the quarrel ended. After learning that Tanchun had persuaded her to leave, he returned from All-Spice Court and admonished Fangguan for a while; only then was peace restored among them all. Now that Fangguan had returned, she said that she wanted some more rose essence for Liu Wu'er. Baoyu promptly replied, “There is some. I hardly drink it myself, so give it all to her.” He told Xiren to bring it out. Seeing that little remained in the bottle, he gave Fangguan the bottle and all.

p.src: Fangguan took the bottle herself and carried it over to them. As it happened, Mrs. Liu had brought her daughter in to relieve her boredom. After strolling for a while around the out-of-the-way corners there, they had returned to the kitchen and were resting over tea. Fangguan arrived with a small glass bottle about five inches high. Holding it up to the light, they saw that it contained somewhat less than half a bottle of rouge-colored liquid and supposed it was the foreign grape wine Baoyu drank. Mother and daughter hurriedly said, “Quick, put some boiling water in the warmer. Sit down for a moment.” Fangguan laughed. “This is all that remains. You may keep the bottle too.” Only then did Wuer realize it was rose essence. She hastily took it and thanked Fangguan again and again. Fangguan asked her again, “Are you feeling better?” “I feel livelier today,” said Wuer, “so I came in to look around. There is nothing very interesting around the back here, though—only some great rocks and trees and the rear walls of the houses. I have not seen any of the truly lovely scenery.” “Why did you not go farther in?” asked Fangguan. Mrs. Liu said, “I told her not to go any farther. The young ladies do not know her, and if someone ill-disposed should see her, it would cause another round of gossip and quarrelling. Once we have entrusted her to your care and she has obtained a post in one of the apartments, there will surely be people to show her around. Indeed, the day may come when she is thoroughly tired of the place.” Fangguan laughed when she heard this. “What is there to fear? She has me.” “Oh, my dear young lady!” Mrs. Liu hastily exclaimed. “We are much more thin-skinned than you people.” As she spoke, she poured another cup of tea. Fangguan had no intention of drinking such tea. She merely rinsed her mouth with a sip and left. Mrs. Liu said, “My hands are occupied here. Wuer, see her out.”

p.src: Wuer escorted Fangguan out. Seeing no one nearby, she caught hold of her and asked, “Did you ever speak about my matter?” Fangguan laughed. “Do you think I would deceive you? I hear there are still two proper vacancies in our apartments, and neither has been filled. One was Hongyu’s place; Second Mistress Lian took her away but has not sent anyone to replace her. The other was Zhuier’s, and that has not been filled either. It would hardly be unreasonable to ask for one of them for you. But Pinger repeatedly tells Xiren that whenever a matter involves moving people or spending money, it is best to postpone it another day if it can be postponed. Third Miss is just now looking for someone to make an example of. She has already rejected two or three matters in her own apartments, and at present she is searching for some fault in ours without having found one. Why deliberately walk into her net? If the request were made and rejected, the refusal would become settled, and it would be difficult to reverse later. It is better to wait until things have cooled down and the Old Lady and Madam are at leisure. However great the matter, if we first speak to our elders then, there is nothing they will not grant.” Wuer said, “That may be so, but I am impatient and cannot bear to wait. If I can be chosen now, first, I can win some credit for Mother and repay her for raising me; second, the extra monthly allowance will make things easier at home; and third, if I can cheer up, perhaps this illness of mine will recover. Then the family would even be spared the expense of summoning doctors and buying medicine.” “I understand it all,” said Fangguan. “Just set your mind at ease.” The two parted, and Fangguan went on her way; nothing more need be said of her for now.

p.src: We now tell only of Wuer, who returned and joined her mother in expressing deep gratitude for Fangguan’s kindness. Her mother said, “I never dreamed we would obtain so much of this. Precious though it is, taking too much of it can easily stir up internal heat. We might as well pour some out and give it to someone. That would be a considerable favor.” “Whom will you give it to?” asked Wuer. Her mother replied, “To your uncle’s son. He had a fever yesterday and was craving something of this sort. I shall pour out half a cup and take it to him now.” Wuer was silent for a long while. She let her mother pour out half a cup, then put the bottle with what remained in the kitchen cupboard. Wuer gave a cold laugh. “If you ask me, it would be better not to give him any at all. If anyone should question us about it, there will be fresh trouble.” Her mother said, “If we started being afraid of such things, how could we ever manage? We work ourselves to the bone; it is only right that we should earn a few things from inside. It is not as though we stole it!” With that, she went straight off. When she reached her elder brother’s home outside, her nephew was lying in bed. At the sight of what she had brought, her brother, sister-in-law, and nephew were all delighted. They immediately drew cool water from the well, mixed him a bowl, and gave it to him. He felt refreshed, and his head and eyes became cool and clear. They covered the remaining half cup with paper and left it on the table.

p.src: By coincidence, several young servants from the household who had long been friendly with her nephew came to inquire after his illness. Among them was a young fellow named Qian Huai, a nephew on Concubine Zhao’s side of the family. His parents were employed keeping accounts at the storehouse, while he himself had been assigned to accompany Jia Huan to school. Since his family had some money and influence and he was still unmarried, he had long admired the pretty Wuer, daughter of the Liu family, and had told his parents that he wanted her for his wife. They had repeatedly asked intermediaries and matchmakers to plead their suit. Wuer’s parents were willing enough, but Wuer herself stubbornly refused. Though she never said so outright, her conduct made her wishes plain, and her parents did not dare accept the proposal. Recently she had set her heart on entering service in the Garden and had put the marriage entirely out of mind, intending to wait until she was released in three or five years and then choose a husband for herself outside. Seeing her attitude, the Qian family let the matter drop. Qian Huai, however, was furious and humiliated at failing to win Wuer. He swore that he would somehow secure her as his match before his desire could be satisfied. Now he too had come with the others to visit the Liu boy, never expecting to find Mrs. Liu there.

u.src: By coincidence, several young servants from the household who had long been friendly with her nephew came to inquire after his illness.
Among them was a young fellow named Qian Huai, a nephew on Concubine Zhao’s side of the family.
His parents were employed keeping accounts at the storehouse, while he himself had been assigned to accompany Jia Huan to school.
Since his family had some money and influence and he was still unmarried, he had long admired the pretty Wuer, daughter of the Liu family, and had told his parents that he wanted her for his wife.
They had repeatedly asked intermediaries and matchmakers to plead their suit.
Wuer’s parents were willing enough, but Wuer herself stubbornly refused. Though she never said so outright, her conduct made her wishes plain, and her parents did not dare accept the proposal.

Recently she had set her heart on entering service in the Garden and had put the marriage entirely out of mind, intending to wait until she was released in three or five years and then choose a husband for herself outside.
Seeing her attitude, the Qian family let the matter drop.
Qian Huai, however, was furious and humiliated at failing to win Wuer. He swore that he would somehow secure her as his match before his desire could be satisfied.
Now he too had come with the others to visit the Liu boy, never expecting to find Mrs. Liu there.

p.src: Mrs. Liu suddenly saw a group of people approaching, among them Qian Huai. Pleading that she had no time to spare, she rose and left. Her brother and sister-in-law hurriedly said, “Auntie, why are you leaving without even having tea? It was so kind of you to think of us.” Mrs. Liu laughed. “I am afraid they may call for the meal inside. I shall come and see my nephew again when I have time.” Her sister-in-law then took a paper packet from a drawer and, holding it in her hand, accompanied Mrs. Liu outside. When they reached the corner of the wall, she handed it to her and said with a smile, “Your brother was on duty at the gate yesterday. Who would have thought that, though his turn comes only once every five days, it would be unusually quiet, without a single gratuity coming his way? Only yesterday, an official from Guangdong came to pay his respects and presented the masters with two small baskets of tuckahoe frost. He also gave the gatekeepers one basket as a gate gift, and this was your brother’s share. That region abounds in thousand-year-old pines and cypresses, so they extract the pure essence of the tuckahoe, blend it with medicines, and somehow produce this remarkably fine white frost. They say the best way is to mix it with human milk and take a small cup every morning, for it is wonderfully nourishing. The next best is cow’s milk, but if neither can be had, plain boiling water will do. We thought it would be just the thing for our niece. Earlier today we sent a little maid to deliver it to your house, but she said the door was locked and that our niece had gone inside the compound too. I had meant to go and see her and take it along myself, but then I thought that, with the masters away and security tight everywhere, and with no errand to attend to, there was no sense in my running about for nothing. Besides, from what I have heard these past two days, everything inside is in an uproar. It would hardly be worthwhile if I became entangled in it. You have come at just the right time, Auntie. Take it to her yourself.”

p.src: Mrs. Liu thanked her for the kindness, took her leave, and headed back. She had just reached the side gate when a young servant boy said with a grin, “Where have you been, ma’am? They have repeatedly sent word from inside asking for you. Three or four of us have been out looking everywhere, yet you still had not returned. And where might you be coming from now? This is not even the road to your home. You have made me suspicious.” Mrs. Liu laughed and scolded him, “You impudent little monkey…” To learn what came of it, please listen to the next chapter.
